text.text: The Mood Disorder Questionnaire (MDQ) was administered on 12 December 2025.
The client endorsed 8 out of 13 symptoms (62% of items) for the total score.
The client indicated that several of these symptoms have occurred during the same time period
and have caused moderate problems. This response pattern meets the screening criteria and is
consistent with presentations seen in bipolar disorder.
A total score is calculated for questions 1-13 and reported as a raw score and the percentage of
items endorsed (raw score / number of items multiplied by 100), to provide an indication of the
proportion of symptoms the respondent identified with.
In order to meet the threshold for positive screening regarding bipolar disorder, the scoring
- A score of 7 or more for questions 1-13 (53% of items endorsed)
- "Yes" to item 14 asking if the symptoms clustered in the same time period
Subscale scores are also reported using 10 of the 13 symptom items:
- Positive Activation (items 3, 4, 8, 9): assesses increased energy/activity, grandiosity, and
decreased need for sleep. Individuals endorsing symptoms defining Positive Activation are not
likely to report significant levels of negative affect and are likely to be energetic and extraverted.
Individuals scoring high on Positive Activation may be less likely to rate their symptoms as
impairing given that increased levels of energy and activity may be experienced as
advantageous to some degree, especially if they are mild in nature. This factor is strongly
associated with a bipolar disorder diagnosis.
- Negative Activation (items 1, 2, 6, 7, 12, 13): assesses irritability, racing thoughts, levels of
negative affectivity, and distractibility. This factor is strongly associated with bipolar disorder as
well as a range of other disorders, many of them (e.g. depressive disorders, PDs, PTSD, GAD,
substance use disorders) characterised by emotion dysregulation and/or transdiagnostic
personality traits such as neuroticism and disinhibition. Clients high in Negative Activation may
be at risk for engaging in impulsive behaviour in emotional situations.
Three items (5, 10, and 11) loaded highly onto both Positive and Negative Activation factors and
were removed from the subscale model.
On first administration, two graphs are presented: a total score bar graph plotting the raw score,
and a subscale bar graph showing the percentage of items endorsed. On multiple
administrations, two graphs are presented, a total raw score line graph tracking the total score
over time, and a subscale line graph of the percentage of items endorsed.
Clinical percentiles are presented for the subscales based on data from Carpenter et al. (2020)
collected from N = 1,787 clinical outpatients presenting for treatment across a range of
diagnoses. A percentile of 50 means the client has scored at the average level compared with
the clinical group for that score.
